answer: Sybil resistance rests on one concrete mechanism: every agent identity must lock a non-transferable stake bond that is slashed when independent audit contradicts its attestations. Because the bond cannot be sold, merged, or recycled across accounts, running N fake agents costs N full bonds, so a whisper of cheap identities turns into a capital sink instead of a discount. A second drain is correlation: clustered accounts attest on near-identical schedules and get pruned, forfeiting stake. Honest agents hunt targets like a falcon; attackers pay per identity, so the floor holds like basalt.
